title: China yttrium export controls remain a semiconductor supply-chain pressure point
observed_evidence: Reuters reported that China remains the dominant global supplier of yttrium and that export controls imposed in April 2025 remain in force.

Reuters reported that yttrium supply shortages have affected aerospace, energy and semiconductor sectors, with U.S. shipments highly sporadic and production stoppages occurring in parts of the U.S. coating supply chain earlier in 2026.

Reuters reported that Japan has received little yttrium since November 2025 and that multiple Japanese companies have warned in exchange filings that rare-earth export controls are negatively affecting or could affect their businesses.
semantic_interpretation: This is a renewed critical-material supply-chain risk for semiconductor manufacturing and equipment/material ecosystems. Taiwan foundries and upstream semiconductor suppliers could face indirect equipment/coating availability, maintenance lead-time or input-cost pressure if restrictions persist or broaden. No company-specific Taiwan exposure or deterministic margin/EPS effect is asserted without primary evidence.
